First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So, we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Rearranging the above identity gives

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{3}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
